title: Final Project
text: All data used in this project is from cBioPortal for Cancer Genomics. The data is from 2023. This source provides data on multiple types of cancer and provides key variables to draw conclusions from.

title: Final Project
text:
Key Variables

Post Sample Immunotherapy: If the patient received immunotherapy after their tumor was studied
Age: Age at the surgery/biopsy
Sex: Male or Female
TP53 Pathway: Whether patient has naturally occurring bodily response to stop tumors from growing
Mutation Count: Number of gene changes found in a tumor
TMB (nonsynonymous): A measure of the DNA changes in cancer cells
Race: White, Black, Asian, Unknown or Uncertain

title: Final Project
text: According to the data, we can see that of you have a higher TMB score, you are more likely to need immunotherapy. This makes sense because since TMB meausres the changes of DNA on a tumor, it should be more likely to for a patient to need a form f immunotherapy if the DNA on their tumor is very different from the DNA in their cells. From this data, we can also see that if you have a higher TMB score, you are more likely to have a TP53 pathway, meaning your body naturally fights against a tumor. This also makes sense because the more variation in the DNA of a tumor, the more likely it should be for your body to recognize that that tumor is bad and try to fight it.

title: Predicting Immunotherapy Use in Patients with Lung Adenocarcinoma Using Demographic and Genomic Characteristics
text: Lung Adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, affecting non-smokers, women and young adults. It primarily affects glandular cells (mucus-making cells) and then spreads to outer parts of the lungs. Tragically, early stages often experience no symptoms, making this type of cancer hard to recognize. This project aims to predict if patients with Lung Adenocarcinoma need immunotherapy using variables like Age, Sex, TP53 Pathway (a natural systrem where cells stop tumors from growing), Mutation Count, TMB (nonsynonymous, predicts the success of immunotherapy), and race.

title: Model
text:
Data Generating Mechanism
The probability \(p_i\) of a patient receiving post-sample immunotherapy is modeled using logistic regression:
\[\text{logit}(p_i) = \ln\left(\frac{p_i}{1 - p_i}\right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1(\text{Age}_i) + \beta_2(\text{Sex}_{\text{Male}, i}) + \beta_3(\text{Race}_{\text{Black}, i}) + \beta_4(\text{Race}_{\text{Other}, i}) + \beta_5(\text{Race}_{\text{Unknown}, i}) + \beta_6(\text{Race}_{\text{White}, i}) + \beta_7(\text{TP53}_{\text{Yes}, i}) + \beta_8(\text{TMB}_i)\]
Using the estimated parameters from our model:
\[\text{logit}(p_i) = -0.794 - 0.0169(\text{Age}_i) - 0.0523(\text{Sex}_{\text{Male}, i}) + 0.460(\text{Race}_{\text{Black}, i}) + 0.476(\text{Race}_{\text{Other}, i}) + 0.667(\text{Race}_{\text{Unknown}, i}) + 0.251(\text{Race}_{\text{White}, i}) + 0.452(\text{TP53}_{\text{Yes}, i}) + 0.0222(\text{TMB}_i)\]

More Plots









We can see from the graph, that there isn’t a clear correlation between age and immunotherapy after surgery/biopsy. However, we can note that most people that did not recieve immunotherapy after surgery/biopsy were between ages 60 and 80. However, the data for people who did recieve immunotherapy after surgery/biopsy is more spread out and doesn’t have a clear age range.
